claims.text: Call weave.init(), then nest start_conversation / start_turn / start_llm / start_tool for the session, each exchange, and the LLM and tool calls inside a turn.
Install weave, call weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]") before any start_* call; agent tracing functions silently no-op if init is missing or tracing is disabled.
The quickstart needs a CoreWeave Forge account and API key, an OpenAI API key, Python 3.10+, and installs `weave openai requests`.

Data model: conversation groups turns, a turn is a user-agent exchange containing LLM calls and the tool executions they trigger; each emits an OTel span tagged with gen_ai.agent.name and gen_ai.conversation.id.
The condensed code sketch shows the quickstart pattern for tracing a multi-turn agent with history, an LLM call, and a tool call.

The quickstart's full version per turn: first start_llm span, start_tool span for each requested tool call, then a second start_llm span for the final answer; history of user, assistant and tool messages is sent each turn.
Each tracing function returns an object that works as a context manager or can be closed with .end().
Traces appear in the Agents tab as a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback; use @weave.op for individual functions.
For supported agent SDKs and harnesses such as the Claude Agent SDK or Codex, Weave can autopatch, so manual instrumentation isn't needed.
I haven't run this against the Weave SDK; I didn't read the start_subagent, manual start/end, or semantic conventions sections in detail.

issues: The code sketch breaks the tool-loop conversation. It appends the assistant message as plain content with no tool_calls. It then appends a role="tool" message with a tool_call_id that has no preceding assistant tool call. This is invalid chat history, and it differs from S7, which appends the full assistant message (model_dump, including tool_calls) before the tool results.

The sketch never sends the tool result back to the model. The second start_llm() is only a comment, and the function returns the first resp.text. The sketch is labeled as condensed. Even so, the code does not do what the surrounding text says: that the quickstart pattern keeps the tool result in history for a second model call.

The tool block runs unconditionally. The comment says "if the model requested a tool", but there is no conditional, and args, args_json and call_id are never defined from the response. S7 gates the tool block on msg.tool_calls and loops over each tool call.

Fix: append the assistant message with its tool_calls, gate the tool block on those tool_calls, and add the second start_llm() call that sends the tool results back to the model. Alternatively, make the sketch a text-only turn and point to S7 for the tool loop.
Revise partial or unsupported material claims.
